reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it centers on reviewing an Airbnb unit and recommending presentation and operational changes to improve its appeal. Although it promotes a course and mentions a high monthly-income figure, the described content focuses on furnishing choices and weak sales, without showing a payment or data request or promising a guaranteed outcome.

opening.argument: The income promise is tied to a concrete participation path, not merely general education. The description advertises earning 10 million won per month from 1 million won and immediately directs viewers to course details, consultation, and an application link. That pairing presents the advertised business outcome as the reason to contact or apply, making this a low-barrier income solicitation rather than a neutral property review.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the segment a review does not answer the direct commercial linkage. The description places a large earnings claim beside course information, consultation, and an application destination. The practical takeaway is not simply how to arrange a room; it is to pursue the advertised business opportunity through the supplied contact path.

The video instead demonstrates room presentation and operational suggestions, including changing props and taking pictures.

opening.argument: Several unusually easy or outsized-return signals reinforce one another: the title claims Airbnb sales can be doubled with five minutes of daily investment, while the description advertises turning 1 million won into 10 million won monthly. These are not modest educational claims; they frame a very small input as producing a dramatic recurring business result, alongside a consultation phone number and application link. The combination warrants treating the promotion as deceptive income acquisition.

The spoken segment openly discusses poor performance, including a student making only 50% sales after opening, and focuses on possible improvements rather than certain returns.

opening.argument: The apparent coaching review is also a direct promotional demonstration. The on-screen banner advertises an Airbnb startup course, a reduced price, and a phone number, while the presenter tells viewers they can start a business and pursue ten million won per month. The property makeover supplies a success-oriented sales narrative: viewers are shown a host, promised a two-times improvement, and then encouraged toward the business opportunity.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The educational framing is precisely what makes the promotion persuasive. The presenter does not merely display a room; she connects her intervention to doubled market share and ends by urging viewers to start the business and reach a stated monthly salary. The review therefore operates as a funnel into the advertised opportunity.

citations.quote: And I will definitely increase your market share by 2 times!
Please start a business.
Be sure to achieve the monthly salary of 10 million won in any way

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The banner and encouragement show promotion, but promotion alone does not establish a scam under the alleged low-barrier-reward theory. The actual demonstration concerns concrete furnishing, cleanliness, lighting, and guest-use changes. It also acknowledges that the unit's sales were poor, which is inconsistent with presenting income as automatic or guaranteed.
